summary: Ian Butler, CEO of Bismouth, delivers a lightning talk on improving vibe coding based on extensive benchmarking of coding agents' bug-finding abilities. Bismouth released the SM100 benchmark covering 100+ repositories and 1200+ issues from multiple agents. The findings are sobering: three out of six agents had 10% or less true positive rate across 900+ reports, Devon and Cursor showed less than 10% true positive rates, and Cursor specifically had a 97% false positive rate. One agent produced 70 issues for a single task, all false positives. This creates alert fatigue and erodes developer trust, leading to bugs reaching production. Butler offers three main improvement strategies. First, bug-focused rules files: feed agents specific security information like the OWASP Top 10, name explicit bug classes (auth bypasses, protocol pollution, SQL injection) rather than vague requests, and require fix validation with passing tests before code integration. Second, context management: agents degrade when context compaction occurs, losing logical links across codebases. Users should feed diffs rather than full files, ensure key files aren't summarized out, and ask agents to produce step-by-step component inventories (classes, variables, usage patterns). Third, thinking models significantly outperform non-thinking models at finding bugs by expanding across considerations and diving deeper via chain of thought. However, even thinking models show high run-to-run variability in which bugs they find, never achieving holistic file analysis. Butler concludes by plugging Bismouth.sh, which automatically creates PRs, integrates with GitHub/GitLab/Jira/Linear, offers vulnerability scanning and code reviews, and supports on-prem deployments. The full SM100 benchmark with methodology and data is available via QR code.

sections.title: Introduction and Benchmark Results
sections.summary: Ian Butler introduces himself as CEO of Bismouth, an end-to-end agentic coding solution. He presents benchmark results showing agents have low bug-finding accuracy: Devon and Cursor have less than 10% true positive rate, three of six agents had 10% or less true positive rate across 900+ reports, and one agent produced 70 false issues for a single task. Cursor specifically had a 97% false positive rate over 100+ repos and 1200+ issues, leading to alert fatigue and bugs reaching production.

sections.title: Three Practical Tips Overview
sections.summary: Butler introduces three strategies for improving vibe coding: bug-focused rules files with scoped instructions for security and logical bugs, context management since agents lose logical links over time, and using thinking models which are significantly better at finding bugs.

sections.title: Bug-Focused Rules Deep Dive
sections.summary: Detailed guidance on rules files: feed specific security information like OWASP Top 10 to bias the model, name explicit bug classes (auth bypasses, protocol pollution, SQL injection) rather than vague requests, and require fix validation with passing tests before code integration. Structured rules eliminate vague 'check for bugs' requests that produce alert fatigue.

sections.title: Context Management Strategies
sections.summary: Agents struggle with cross-repo navigation and bug detection degrades significantly during context compaction. Users should feed diffs of changed code, ensure key files aren't summarized out of context, and ask agents to produce step-by-step component inventories (classes, variables, usage patterns) to improve bug-finding ability.

sections.title: Thinking Models Performance and Limitations
sections.summary: Thinking models significantly outperform non-thinking models by expanding across considerations and diving deeper via chain of thought. However, even thinking models show high run-to-run variability—topline bug counts remain similar but specific bugs found change each run. Agents never holistically examine files like humans do, a major current limitation.

sections.title: Bismouth Product Plug and Conclusion
sections.summary: Butler plugs Bismouth.sh, which automatically creates PRs and integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, and Linear. It offers vulnerability scanning, code reviews, and on-prem deployments. A QR code links to the full SM100 benchmark with methodology, results, and explorable dataset.
